newsitem.title: USA: Digital sues Intel over patents.
newsitem.headline: Digital sues Intel over patents.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp. said on Tuesday it is suing Intel Corp. for allegedly infringing patents on 10 of its computer chip products.
News of the suit sent Intel's stock down $3.375 to $155.875 on Nasdaq. Digital rose $1.50 to $34.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The suit, filed in a federal district court in Massachusetts, charges that Intel "willfully infringed" the patents in making, using and selling products from Intel's Pentium, Pentium Pro and Pentium II microprocessor families.
As a result, "Intel has strengthened its monopoly in the X86 market and is seeking to extend its monopoly to higher-performance microprocessors," said Chairman Robert Palmer.
Intel officials were not immediately available to comment.
The powerful Pentium and X86 computer chips are a major force in driving the demand for new computer purchases.
The suit alleges that Intel's patent infringement caused Digital economic injury that would cause irreparable harm if not stopped, the Worcester, Mass.-based company said.
It seeks an injunction to prohibit Intel from using Digital's patented technology in Intel's present and future microprocessor products, as well as triple monetary damages.
Digital said the patents, issued between 1988 and 1996, protect its innovations in high-performance computing architecture and microprocessor technology.
